institution: ICMR multicentric ESBL study (AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER, CMC Vellore, JIPMER)

verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026)

notes: Source: Gautam et al, Indian J Med Res 2019;149:208-215 (ICMR multi-centric ESBL study, 4 tertiary centres: AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry; Oct 2014-Mar 2016). Study covers ONLY E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304 isolates) — no P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, S. aureus, or Enterococcus. Method: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion, CLSI. Table II reports % SUSCEPTIBLE by centre; Table III reports % RESISTANT (n/N) split by ESBL-producer vs non-ESBL. I derived OVERALL susceptibility by pooling Table III ESBL + non-ESBL resistant counts per drug (s = 100 - pooled %R, from_R:true for all pooled cells). Colistin values taken directly from the printed overall figures in the Results text (E. coli 99% = 271/274; K. pneumoniae 98% = 229/234), not from R. CAVEAT: Table III denominators (e.g. 167+202=369 for E. coli, 98+126=224 for K. pneumoniae) exceed stated collection totals of 341/304, likely reflecting drug-specific tested subsets/classification; per-drug pooled %R is nevertheless computed directly from printed n/N. Individual per-centre susceptibility values are available in Table II if centre-level breakdown is preferred. ESBL prevalence context: CDT dete
